headline: An AI search of the largest 2D map of the universe has found 70 new gravitational lenses.
score_reason: Confirmed astronomy result in a published journal study; a useful research item, not a major event.
importance_line: It adds 70 confirmed cases to a catalogue that astronomers can use for years to study dark matter and the expansion of the universe, and it shows AI finding rare objects that would be too slow to search for by eye.
summary: NSF NOIRLab, in a release carried by Newswise, reports that an international team used AI to find 70 new gravitational lenses in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, a large sky map. Gravitational lenses are massive objects that bend and magnify the light of more distant objects, acting as natural telescopes that can help scientists study dark matter and the early universe.
notes: Read in full from Newswise. The institution as first reporter (NSF NOIRLab) is inferred from the release's image credits and staff quotes; Nanowerk (pool source) is a copy site and was blocked here. Named with position: Xiaosheng Huang (Santa Clara University and DOE's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) led the machine-learning search; Aleksandar Cikota (Associate Scientist, NSF NOIRLab) is a co-author and leads the follow-up observing program.
